professors.name: Dr. Amara Khan
professors.bio: Researches databases and data-intensive systems. Teaches CS 210 and CS 350.

reviews.text: Dr. Khan explains SQL and relational algebra so clearly. Her lectures are engaging and she is incredibly helpful during office hours. The assignments are fair and well-structured.
Best professor I've had in the CS department. Clear explanations, fair grading, and genuinely cares about students. Highly recommend.
Took CS 210 with Khan last semester. Workload was manageable, the projects were actually interesting, and she was very responsive on Piazza.
Khan is one of the good ones. Her OS class is hard but fair — you will actually learn a ton if you put in the effort.
Lectures can be dense but she's approachable and supportive. Exams were tough but graded fairly.
Honestly one of the best lecturers in the department. She makes database theory feel intuitive.

professors.name: Prof. Daniel Morrison
professors.bio: Algebraic topology; teaches Calculus I and Linear Algebra.

reviews.text: Lectures are monotone and confusing. He rushes through examples and the homework is overwhelming. Not a great experience.
Morrison's exams are unfair. Nothing on them looks like what we did in class. Workload is heavy and grading is strict.
He knows the material deeply but his teaching style is dry. If you're motivated you'll be fine, otherwise it's rough.
Honestly a boring professor. Lectures feel disorganized. You're better off studying from the textbook.
Unhelpful during office hours — he seems annoyed when you ask questions. Grading is harsh.
Incredible professor. She is enthusiastic, inspiring, and genuinely invested in her students' success. Office hours are extremely helpful.
Raman is a gem. Her explanations are crystal clear and her assignments are actually fun. The best intro class I've taken.
Fair grader, engaging lectures, supportive TA team. Workload is reasonable and you learn a lot.
She's passionate about teaching and it shows. Highly recommend taking her section.
Extremely approachable and clear. I felt comfortable asking questions. Exams were fair.
Mixed experience. Lectures are engaging when he's prepared but some days feel rushed. Assignments are heavy but fair.
Whittaker is fine. Not the best, not the worst. The workload is manageable if you start early.
Grading is a bit strict but exams are predictable. He's helpful during office hours.
Dry lectures but he knows his stuff. You'll pass if you do the problem sets.
Lin is engaging and explains complex microeconomic models with clarity. Very fair grader and supportive.
Took ECON 201 with her and loved it. Her lectures tie theory to real-world examples in a way that's genuinely interesting.
Clear, organized, and approachable. Homework is light but meaningful.
Honestly one of the better profs in the department. Responsive to emails and office hours are actually helpful.
Condescending and unapproachable. Grading feels biased — comments are harsh and not constructive.
Avoid if you can. Lectures are dull, grading is unfair, and he's dismissive of questions in class.
Workload is heavy and the rubrics are vague. Feedback is minimal.
Not helpful during office hours. The class itself is not worth the stress.
Engaging lectures with lots of real-world examples. Fair exams and a supportive TA team.
Okafor is great. Her enthusiasm for the material is contagious. Assignments are reasonable.
Clear explanations, approachable, and genuinely caring. Office hours are very helpful.
Brilliant but disorganized. The material is interesting, but the pacing is inconsistent and the project specs are vague.
Rossi knows his stuff but expect a heavy workload. Grading was a bit strict on me but I learned a lot.
Lectures are engaging when he's on topic. Assignments are challenging and time-consuming.
Fair overall. He'll help you if you show up to office hours prepared.
